text:
B: Alright! Can you hear me okay? Sorry if there's music, there's a nail bar under my flat.
A: Yeah, I can hear it. I'm Kerry.
B: Callum. Where are you, then?
A: Washington. Near Sunderland.
B: Oh, proper north. I'm Catford, South London. What d'you do?
A: Team leader at a contact centre. Broadband and TV.
B: Is that the lanyard in your photo? Sorry, I clocked it, I thought you were still at work.
A: I'd just got in from a shift, to be honest. I forget I've got it on half the time.
B: Long shifts, then?
A: Fifty, fifty-five hours some weeks with overtime. I've got fourteen advisors and I take all the escalations, so when somebody's shouting they get put through to me.
B: Nah, I couldn't do that. I'd just hang up on them.
A: You can't hang up. You let them have their rant, then you sort it. Most people just want to know somebody's actually listening.
B: Fair. That's kind of like events, though, innit. Someone's always kicking off about the sound or the guest list, and you've got to keep it calm.
A: What events?
B: I do production work. Warehouse parties, setting up the rigs, lights, all that. And I'm at uni, media and comms.
A: Right. Is that full-time, the uni?
B: Yeah, second year. Well, full-time on paper, you get me.
A: Meaning you don't go.
B: Ha, nah, I go! Mostly. Some of the lectures are a bit dead, to be fair.
A: I've got lads like that at work. Always a reason why they've not done it.
B: Nah, nah, see, the thing is, that's different. If it's a job you've got to turn up, obviously. Uni's more, like, you're paying, so it's your choice.
A: Still your money, though, isn't it. I left college in my second year to go full-time, so I'm not one to talk, to be honest.
B: What were you doing?
A: BTEC in business, at Sunderland College. I needed the wage. I did my NVQ through work after.
B: See, that's what I'm saying, you don't need the degree to do alright. You're a manager now.
A: Team leader. It's not the same money, believe me. I'm after operations manager in a few years.
B: You'll get it. You've got the vibe.
A: What vibe?
B: Like, nobody's messing you about.
A: Ha. Fair enough. What do you do when you're not at parties, then?
B: Films, mostly. Korean thrillers, that kind of thing. Making beats. You?
A: Reality telly. Married at First Sight, Love Island. Crime documentaries on Netflix.
B: Oh, the crime ones are decent, actually. Which ones?
A: Whatever's new, to be honest. I'm not fussy. I walk the dog and I watch telly, that's about it.
B: What dog?
A: Staffy, Tia. She eats the settee.
B: Staffies are sound. Everyone thinks they're scary.
A: Soft as anything, she is.
